name: XAIGrokVoice
title: xAI Grok Voice
description: Realtime voice conversation with xAI's Grok
whenToUse: Hold a spoken, two-way conversation with Grok in real time: the person talks, Grok answers aloud, and either can interrupt the other. Pick it when the interaction is a VOICE CALL rather than text, and when you want xAI's model. It consumes tools from MCP provider nodes attached via service edges.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: Trigger. Starting the node opens the call.

outputs.name: text
outputs.description: The last completed turn: { query, response }

outputs.name: sessionReady
outputs.description: True once the vendor accepted the handshake

outputs.name: userTranscript
outputs.description: What the person said, per completed utterance

outputs.name: assistantTranscript
outputs.description: What Grok said, accumulated as it speaks

model.title: Model
model.description: Which model answers the call. Think Fast 2 is the flagship; Latest silently follows whatever xAI promotes next, so pin the version when behavior must not change under you.

systemPrompt.title: System Prompt
systemPrompt.description: System instructions for Grok. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.markdownGuidelines}}.

initialRequest.title: Initial Request
initialRequest.description: Text sent as a user message at call start — Grok answers it immediately.

scriptedOpening.title: Scripted Opening
scriptedOpening.description: Spoken word-for-word before the conversation starts, and cannot be interrupted. Use for wording that must never be paraphrased, like a recording disclosure.

languageHint.title: Language Hint
languageHint.description: Biases what the caller is understood in, as a BCP-47 code like ar or ja. Leave empty and the language is auto-detected per utterance.

keyterms.title: Key Terms
keyterms.description: Words the caller is likely to say that transcription would otherwise miss — product names, acronyms, jargon. An array of up to 100 strings.

pronunciation.title: Pronunciation
pronunciation.description: Fixes how Grok SAYS a phrase without changing what it writes: a map from the written form to how it should sound, like {"Yas Island": "Yahs Island"}.

turnDetection.title: Turn Detection
turnDetection.description: How Grok decides the person has finished speaking. Manual disables detection entirely, so nothing is answered unless something else commits the audio buffer.

reasoningEffort.title: Reasoning
reasoningEffort.description: Whether Grok deliberates before speaking. None answers fastest at the cost of harder questions; High is the vendor default.

conversationHistory.title: Conversation History
conversationHistory.description: Array of prior turns ({ role, content }), replayed into the session before the call starts

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: xai-grok
package.packageFile:
$schema: ../_schema/package.schema.json

# XAI GROK, fully declarative.
#
# The node is a REALTIME VOICE session, not a text agent — `wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime` — so what
# unblocked it was `transport: ws` and the audio lane, built for openai-realtime. Its protocol is
# identical to OpenAI's realtime format event for event, which is why shared/tools.yaml reads the same.
#
# TWO SOCKETS ARE INVOLVED and only one is here: the vendor socket is this manifest's `run`, while the
# platform's audio socket to the browser is api/audio.yaml. That second lane exists only because MCP
# cannot carry binary audio; everything else this node emits reaches the client over MCP streaming.

name: xai-grok
displayName: xAI Grok
description: Voice conversations, image generation and video generation with xAI's Grok
# 2.1.0: grok-voice-think-fast-2.0 (model picker + reasoning dial + gated transcription), plus the
# transcript-accumulation and Q/A-log fixes proven live on the sibling realtime voice node.
# 2.2.0: Grok Imagine joins the package — XAIGrokImage (imagine-image-2.0, synchronous) and
# XAIGrokVideo (imagine-video-1.5, an async job the poll capability waits on).
# 2.3.0: XAIGrokVideoExtend — chained shots via /v1/videos/extensions, because one 15-second
# generation compresses a construction-to-function arc too far (probed live 2026-08-15).
version: 2.3.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1777865512/gravity/icons/X_logo.jpg

features:
  - Realtime voice conversation with Grok, with MCP tool calling
  - Image generation with Grok Imagine, typography-strong, hosted URLs back
  - Short video generation from a prompt or a still image, with sound
  - Video extension, continuing an existing clip shot by shot

allowedHosts:
  - api.x.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  # ws carries the voice session; json carries the Imagine REST calls.
  transport: [ws, json]
  # The video node waits on a render job. Without `poll` it would settle on the job RECEIPT
  # and emit that as the answer, with nothing anywhere reporting a problem.
  poll: true

credentials.xaiCredential.yaml:
$schema: ../../_schema/credential.schema.json

name: xaiCredential
displayName: xAI
description: Credentials for xAI Grok API
documentationUrl: https://console.x.ai

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your xAI API key
    placeholder: xai-

shared.tools.yaml:
# The xAI Grok REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   no toolsInto     Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST. A realtime session declares it
#                    ONCE in the handshake, so there is no request field to name; run.yaml reads
#                    `services.mcpService.tools` into session.update itself.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# HOW THE LIST IS RE-OFFERED once it has grown mid-call. A socket sends its tools once at the
# handshake, so growth has to be announced on purpose — this message is that announcement.
#
# ONLY `tools` in the session block: session.update MERGES rather than replaces (verified live on
# OpenAI 2026-08-12; xAI documents the same session.update semantics), so instructions, voice and
# turn detection survive untouched. Re-sending the whole session would be a second copy of the
# handshake, free to drift. No `type: realtime` key — xAI's session object does not carry one.
offer: >-
  return { type: 'session.update', session: { tools: tools } }

# HOW THE INSTRUCTIONS ARE RE-SENT when a region skill comes into force or is cleared. The same
# shape and the same reason as `offer`, for the other thing the handshake sent once: a skill is
# decided by WHERE the conversation is standing, so it can change at any moment, and a socket
# that never mentions it again leaves the model working to a prompt that no longer describes
# where it is.
#
# ONLY `instructions`, for the merge reason above. The configured prompt is repeated alongside
# `skillsText` because a merge REPLACES the field it names: sending the skills alone would drop
# the node's role. No `type: realtime` key, matching `offer`.
reinstruct: >-
  return { type: 'session.update',
           session: { instructions: config.systemPrompt + skillsText } }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]

files.api/audio.yaml:
$schema: ../../../../_schema/audio.schema.json

# THE AUDIO LANE. The platform's socket to the browser, not the vendor's.
#
# It exists for ONE reason: MCP cannot carry binary audio. Everything else this node produces is in
# events.yaml and reaches the client over MCP streaming. Nothing non-audio belongs here.
#
# Every key NAMES computation the executor does. The resampling, the coalescing and the barge-in discard
# are identical for every vendor, which is exactly why they are not written out here.
#
# IDENTICAL TO THE OPENAI VOICE NODE'S, because xAI uses the same realtime event names. That is worth
# stating rather than leaving as a coincidence: if xAI ever renames one of these, this file changes and
# no other node is touched.

in:
  # Grok wants 24 kHz; the browser captures 16 kHz. Getting this wrong is not an error anywhere — the
  # model simply hears a chipmunk, and it reads as poor accuracy.
  resampleTo: 24000
  message:
    type: input_audio_buffer.append
    audio: "{{ audio.base64 }}"

out:
  match: response.output_audio.delta
  value: "return response.delta"
  # Flushes what is buffered and THEN signals the end. The order is the executor's guarantee: a frame
  # sent after the end-of-utterance lands on a player that has already stopped.
  done: response.output_audio.done
  # BARGE-IN. Buffered audio is DISCARDED rather than flushed, because the person is already talking
  # over the sentence it belongs to.
  interruptOn: input_audio_buffer.speech_started

control:
  # The person pressing hang up. Without this the call only ends when the vendor times out. `stop` is
  # the code version's own second name for it.
  endOn: [END_CALL, stop]

  # THE VENDOR'S VOICE-ACTIVITY DETECTION, forwarded so the client can show that it is listening.
  #
  # `userSpeaking` names the SAME event as `out.interruptOn`, which is deliberate rather than duplicated:
  # one tells the client the person started talking, the other throws away the assistant audio they
  # talked over. Two jobs that happen to share a trigger.
  userSpeaking: input_audio_buffer.speech_started
  userStopped: input_audio_buffer.speech_stopped
files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.
#
# EVERYTHING HERE REACHES THE CLIENT OVER MCP STREAMING by landing on an output connector. Only audio
# needs the separate lane, and audio is not in this file.

# THE CODE VERSION'S SHAPE: { query, response } for the last completed turn.
#
# `from: complete` because ONE row sees ONE event and this needs two — the person's transcript and the
# model's arrive separately. `complete` fires once at the end over everything already emitted, which is
# the only place both are in scope together.
- emit: text
  from: complete
  value: >-
    return {
      query: (events.filter(e => e.emit === 'userTranscript').map(e => e.value).at(-1)) ?? '',
      response: (events.filter(e => e.emit === 'assistantTranscript').map(e => e.value).at(-1)) ?? ''
    }

# `from: tool` — NOT from the socket. A tool result is produced by the platform running the tool and
# never appears in the vendor's stream, so no `match` could catch it.
- emit: mcpResult
  from: tool
  value: "return { name: call.name, args: call.args, output: call.output }"

# The Q/A log, in the code version's format ("Q1: …\nA1: …\n"), composed at the end because the
# two halves of a turn arrive on different events.
#
# COUNTING EMISSIONS, NOT TURNS, was the bug found live on the sibling voice node (2026-08-12):
# `assistantTranscript` is accumulate + throttle, so one sentence lands in `events` as a dozen
# longer snapshots of itself, and numbering by index gave a line per snapshot. Two passes fix it:
# COLLAPSE a run of consecutive rows to the value it settled on, then UNPREFIX (the accumulator
# grows across the call, so each value is a strict prefix of the next; guarded by startsWith for
# barge-in, where it isn't). Q and A are counted separately because a call can open with the
# assistant speaking and the two sides then never re-align.
- emit: progress
  from: complete
  value: >-
    return events.filter(e => e.emit === 'userTranscript' || e.emit === 'assistantTranscript')
      .reduce((turns, e) => turns.length && turns.at(-1).emit === e.emit
        ? turns.slice(0, -1).concat([e])
        : turns.concat([e]), [])
      .reduce((out, e) => {
        const user = e.emit === 'userTranscript';
        const value = String(e.value ?? '');
        const said = !user && out.spoken && value.startsWith(out.spoken)
          ? value.slice(out.spoken.length)
          : value;
        return {
          spoken: user ? out.spoken : value,
          q: user ? out.q + 1 : out.q,
          a: user ? out.a : out.a + 1,
          log: out.log + (user ? 'Q' + (out.q + 1) : 'A' + (out.a + 1)) + ': ' + said.trim() + '\n'
        };
      }, { spoken: '', q: 0, a: 0, log: '' })
      .log

# The handshake was accepted — the node's own liveness signal, and the one thing a fixture can prove
# without a microphone. A REJECTED handshake would otherwise look exactly like a quiet call.
- emit: sessionReady
  match: session.updated
  value: "return true"

# v2 GATES TRANSCRIPTION: this event only arrives when run.yaml names `grok-transcribe` as the
# input transcription model, which it now does. (v2 also streams a cumulative
# `...transcription.updated` mid-utterance; `completed` is the settled per-utterance text and is
# the one a turn is made of.)
#
# AN EMPTY TRANSCRIPTION IS NOT A TURN, which is what `when` is here to say: the vendor sends
# `completed` with an empty transcript when it heard speech it could not resolve into words, and
# emitting that fired a user turn nobody took — { query: "", ... } and a blank Q line (observed
# live on the sibling voice node, 2026-08-12). Skipping the row, not `|| ''` in value, is what
# says "they did not speak".
- emit: userTranscript
  match: conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed
  when: "return String(response.transcript || '').trim().length > 0"
  value: "return response.transcript"

# ACCUMULATED, so a consumer gets the sentence so far rather than a syllable, and throttled because the
# vendor sends a delta every few characters.
#
# RESET AT THE END OF EACH TURN, which on a socket is not optional: accumulation runs for the
# length of the RUN, and this node's run is the whole CALL. Without `resetOn` every turn carries
# every turn before it — the sibling voice node showed exactly that live (2026-08-12), with
# `text.response` settling as the entire conversation concatenated. `response.done` and not
# `response.output_audio_transcript.done`, because the turn is over when the RESPONSE is, and a
# response may carry more than one output item.
- emit: assistantTranscript
  match: response.output_audio_transcript.delta
  value: "return response.delta || ''"
  accumulate: true
  throttleMs: 200
  resetOn: response.done
files.api/run.yaml:
# ONE duplex session. Not a request: this stays open for the length of the call, and the node's run IS
# the call.
#
# The bearer token goes on the HANDSHAKE, resolved by the same auth code an HTTP call uses rather than a
# second copy of it.
#
# THE MODEL COMES FROM CONFIG since the think-fast-2.0 upgrade (2026-08-15). The v1 manifest fixed it
# because a free-text value the endpoint rejects fails the whole call at handshake time; config.yaml
# now enum-constrains it to the vendor's own list, which removes that risk without hardcoding an id
# that goes stale — exactly the OpenAI voice node's arrangement.

- name: session
  transport: ws
  url: "return 'wss://api.x.ai/v1/realtime?model=' + config.model"
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.xaiCredential.apiKey }}"

  # THE HANDSHAKE. A list because it is a list for other vendors — Nova needs an ordered sequence — and
  # Grok, like OpenAI, needs one message plus the optional replay and opening prompt below.
  #
  # FLATTER THAN OPENAI'S: no output_modalities, no transcription model, no noise reduction, no token
  # ceiling. Transcribed from SessionUpdateBuilder rather than copied from the OpenAI node, because
  # sending fields a vendor does not document is how a handshake gets rejected.
  open:
    - type: session.update
      session:
        instructions: "{{ config.systemPrompt }}"
        voice: "{{ config.voice }}"
        # THE THINKING DIAL, new with think-fast-2.0. `high` is the vendor default; `none` trades
        # reasoning for latency. Sent even at the default so the session states what it runs at.
        reasoning: "return { effort: config.reasoningEffort || 'high' }"
        # HOW A PHRASE SOUNDS, not what it writes — the vendor's `replace` map, applied at the
        # mouth. Transcripts and the conversation keep the written form.
        replace: "return config.pronunciation || {}"
        # `null` DISABLES turn detection, which is the vendor's own spelling and not a template
        # accident. With it null nothing ever decides the person has finished speaking, so nothing is
        # answered unless something else commits the buffer.
        #
        # NO HAND-TUNED THRESHOLDS since 2.0. The v1 numbers (0.6 / 300ms / 600ms) were tuned against
        # the v1 model; 2.0 ships its own defaults (threshold 0.85, prefix 333ms) tuned against
        # itself, and re-sending v1's numbers would silently override them. Bare `server_vad` takes
        # whatever the current model considers right.
        turn_detection: >-
          return config.turnDetection === 'manual' ? null : { type: 'server_vad' }
        audio:
          # 24 kHz both ways. The browser captures at 16 kHz and the executor resamples, named in
          # api/audio.yaml because interpolation is not something an expression can express.
          input:
            format: { type: audio/pcm, rate: 24000 }
            # GATES the streaming user transcript. v2 only emits the input transcription events when
            # a transcription model is named; without the model line the person's words never come
            # back and userTranscript stays silent for the whole call.
            #
            # The hint and the terms bias UNDERSTANDING of the caller, not what Grok speaks:
            # `language_hint` says what language to expect (auto-detected when empty), `keyterms`
            # (up to 100) are the domain words transcription would otherwise miss. `undefined`
            # drops the key from the JSON, which is how "not set" stays unsent.
            transcription: >-
              return {
                model: 'grok-transcribe',
                language_hint: String(config.languageHint || '').trim() || undefined,
                keyterms: (config.keyterms || []).length ? config.keyterms : undefined
              }
          output: { format: { type: audio/pcm, rate: 24000 } }

        # TOOLS ARE DECLARED ONCE, HERE, because a realtime session has no per-request moment to offer
        # them. The executor discovers them from the wired MCP provider before the handshake and puts
        # them in the ordinary consumer root, so this reads like any other consumer. Empty when nothing
        # is wired — the normal case — and the call degrades to plain voice.
        tools: "return services.mcpService.tools || []"
        tool_choice: "return (services.mcpService.tools || []).length ? 'auto' : 'none'"

    # HISTORY, replayed before the call starts. One entry resolving to an ARRAY, so a variable number of
    # turns is expressible; an empty history resolves to [] and sends nothing.
    #
    # The roles use DIFFERENT content types, which is the vendor's rule and easy to get wrong: a user
    # message carries `input_text`, an assistant message carries `text`.
    - >-
      return (config.conversationHistory || []).map(m => ({
        type: 'conversation.item.create',
        item: {
          type: 'message',
          role: m.role === 'assistant' ? 'assistant' : 'user',
          content: [{ type: m.role === 'assistant' ? 'text' : 'input_text', text: String(m.content ?? '') }]
        }
      }))

    # THE SCRIPTED LINE, spoken before anything conversational. The vendor's force_message item
    # reads the text VERBATIM — no generation, so compliance wording cannot be paraphrased — and
    # `interruptible: false` means it cannot be talked over. No `response.create` after it: a
    # forced line is not a turn and asks for no answer. Before the opening prompt below, so a call
    # with both plays script first, then the generated greeting. [] when empty.
    - >-
      return String(config.scriptedOpening || '').trim()
        ? [{ type: 'conversation.item.create',
             item: { type: 'force_message', role: 'assistant', interruptible: false,
                     content: [{ type: 'output_text', text: String(config.scriptedOpening) }] } }]
        : []

    # THE OPENING PROMPT. Two messages: the user's, then `response.create` so the model answers it at
    # once. Without the second the item sits in the conversation and Grok never speaks, which defeats
    # the point of the field. Resolves to [] when empty, so a call with no opening prompt just waits.
    - >-
      return String(config.initialRequest || '').trim()
        ? [
            { type: 'conversation.item.create',
              item: { type: 'message', role: 'user',
                      content: [{ type: 'input_text', text: String(config.initialRequest) }] } },
            { type: 'response.create' }
          ]
        : []

  # No `close` list: xAI ends the session cleanly on socket close, and sending something first would be
  # inventing a message the vendor does not document.
files.api/toolExchange.yaml:
# xAI's realtime tool protocol, imported whole. Identical to OpenAI's realtime format, which is xAI's
# choice rather than a shortcut taken here — see shared/tools.yaml.
$ref: tools

# maxTurns and stuckAfterRepeats are MEANINGLESS on a socket and deliberately absent. A turn budget
# describes an HTTP loop that sends a request and reads a reply; a realtime session never ends a turn,
# so a tool result goes back down the same open connection. The duplex path resolves calls inline.
files.config.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/config.schema.json

configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model]
  properties:
    # ENUM-CONSTRAINED, which is what makes exposing it safe: the v1 node fixed the model in
    # run.yaml because a free-text value the endpoint rejects fails the whole call at handshake
    # time. Both values are the vendor's own (docs.x.ai realtime schema, 2026-08-15), so a picker
    # cannot produce a rejected handshake. `grok-voice-latest` is the vendor alias and has routed
    # to 2.0 since 2026-08-05 — pinning 2.0 is the default so a future silent re-route is a
    # choice here, not a surprise. think-fast-1.0 is deliberately NOT offered: superseded, and
    # keeping it would only preserve a way to pick the worse call.
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: >-
        Which model answers the call. Think Fast 2 is the flagship; Latest silently follows
        whatever xAI promotes next, so pin the version when behavior must not change under you.
      enum: [grok-voice-think-fast-2.0, grok-voice-latest]
      enumNames: [Think Fast 2.0, Latest (xAI alias)]
      default: grok-voice-think-fast-2.0
    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: System Prompt
      description: System instructions for Grok. Shared blocks work here, e.g. {{prompt.markdownGuidelines}}.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    initialRequest:
      type: string
      title: Initial Request
      description: Text sent as a user message at call start — Grok answers it immediately.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    # DIFFERENT from initialRequest, and both can be set: initialRequest makes the model GENERATE
    # an answer, this makes it READ a line verbatim. Verbatim is the point — compliance wording
    # ("this call is recorded") must never be paraphrased, so it rides the vendor's force_message
    # item, which speaks the text exactly and cannot be talked over.
    scriptedOpening:
      type: string
      title: Scripted Opening
      description: >-
        Spoken word-for-word before the conversation starts, and cannot be interrupted. Use for
        wording that must never be paraphrased, like a recording disclosure.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    languageHint:
      type: string
      title: Language Hint
      description: >-
        Biases what the caller is understood in, as a BCP-47 code like ar or ja. Leave empty and
        the language is auto-detected per utterance.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    keyterms:
      type: object
      title: Key Terms
      description: >-
        Words the caller is likely to say that transcription would otherwise miss — product names,
        acronyms, jargon. An array of up to 100 strings.
      "ui:field": template
    pronunciation:
      type: object
      title: Pronunciation
      description: >-
        Fixes how Grok SAYS a phrase without changing what it writes: a map from the written form
        to how it should sound, like {"Yas Island": "Yahs Island"}.
      "ui:field": template
    voice:
      type: string
      title: Voice
      description: The voice Grok speaks with
      enum: [eve, ara, rex, sal, leo]
      enumNames: [Eve, Ara, Rex, Sal, Leo]
      default: eve
    turnDetection:
      type: string
      title: Turn Detection
      description: >-
        How Grok decides the person has finished speaking. Manual disables detection entirely, so
        nothing is answered unless something else commits the audio buffer.
      enum: [server_vad, manual]
      enumNames: ["Server VAD (automatic)", Manual]
      default: server_vad
    # v2 IS A THINKING MODEL — "think fast" is the product name, and effort is the one dial the
    # vendor exposes. `none` trades reasoning for latency; the vendor default is high.
    reasoningEffort:
      type: string
      title: Reasoning
      description: >-
        Whether Grok deliberates before speaking. None answers fastest at the cost of harder
        questions; High is the vendor default.
      enum: [high, none]
      enumNames: [High (default), None (fastest)]
      default: high
    conversationHistory:
      type: object
      title: Conversation History
      description: Array of prior turns ({ role, content }), replayed into the session before the call starts
      "ui:field": template
"ui:order":
  [model, systemPrompt, scriptedOpening, initialRequest, voice, turnDetection, reasoningEffort, languageHint, keyterms, pronunciation, conversationHistory]
files.interface.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/interface.schema.json

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: Trigger. Starting the node opens the call.
    required: false

# THE SAME SIX OUTPUTS AS THE OTHER REALTIME VOICE NODE, by decision (2026-08-15): the two nodes
# are drop-in swaps for each other, and identical connectors is what makes the swap mechanical.
# `conversation` (the accumulated full call) was the one extra and was removed for that parity —
# `progress` carries the same turns as text.
outputs:
  - name: text
    type: object
    description: "The last completed turn: { query, response }"
  - name: mcpResult
    type: object
    description: MCP tool results
  - name: progress
    type: string
    description: Q/A log of the call

  # ADDED, not renamed. The code version kept the call's transcripts inside itself and only ever emitted
  # the assembled `text` and `progress`. A manifest cannot do that: one events row sees ONE event, and
  # the person's transcript and the model's arrive on different ones — so they have to land on
  # connectors before anything can compose them.
  #
  # Additive, so no saved workflow notices, and useful on their own: a live caption needs the assistant
  # transcript as it streams, not the finished turn.
  - name: sessionReady
    type: boolean
    description: True once the vendor accepted the handshake
  - name: userTranscript
    type: string
    description: What the person said, per completed utterance
  - name: assistantTranscript
    type: string
    description: What Grok said, accumulated as it speaks

credentials:
  - name: xaiCredential
    required: true
    displayName: xAI

serviceConnectors:
  - name: mcpService
    description: MCP service connector — automatic schema discovery
    serviceType: mcp
    isService: false
files.node.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/node.schema.json

type: XAIGrokVoice
# A CallbackNode because the session STREAMS for the length of the call. Derived from
# `transport: ws` and verified by lint, not taken on trust.
kind: CallbackNode

name: xAI Grok Voice
# The JOB is a voice call, and Voice is one of the twelve categories (node-discoverability.md).
# `AI` pulled this toward text-model vocabulary and away from the work; the other realtime voice
# node already sits in Voice.
category: Voice
color: "#000000"
# The X logo the legacy Grok node carried, shared with the x-search package.
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1777865512/gravity/icons/X_logo.jpg

description: Realtime voice conversation with xAI's Grok

whenToUse: >-
  Hold a spoken, two-way conversation with Grok in real time: the person talks, Grok answers aloud, and
  either can interrupt the other. Pick it when the interaction is a VOICE CALL rather than text, and
  when you want xAI's model. It consumes tools from MCP provider nodes attached via service edges.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A live conversation is never cacheable: the answer depends on what was just said.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
$schema: ../../../_schema/test.schema.json

# WHAT A FIXTURE CAN PROVE ABOUT A VOICE CALL, which is less than for any other node: there is no
# microphone on the bench and no browser to send audio to, so the only decidable question is whether the
# vendor ACCEPTED the handshake.
#
# That is worth asserting on its own. A rejected handshake — a bad key, an unknown voice, a malformed
# session — looks exactly like a quiet call from the outside, which is the failure that cost a day on the
# OpenAI voice node. `sessionReady` fires on session.updated and is the node's own liveness signal.
#
# Running it live needs XAI_API_KEY.

testData:
  config:
    model: grok-voice-think-fast-2.0
    systemPrompt: You are a concise assistant. Keep answers to one sentence.
    initialRequest: Say hello and nothing else.
    voice: eve
    turnDetection: server_vad
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    sessionReady: "return output.sessionReady === true"
